newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cricket-Warne keen to increase workload.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cricket-Warne keen to increase workload.

text.p: Leg-spinner Shane Warne said on the eve of his first major cricket match in six months that he wants to test his injured finger with long bowling spells.

"At this stage I'm not too concerned about the wickets and how many runs I go for," Warne told reporters during training for the Sheffield Shield match between Victoria and New South Wales which starts on Friday.
"I'm just worried about ripping them and turning them and seeing how (the finger) pulls up the next day," Warne said on Wednesday.

Warne, who underwent surgery on the ring finger of his right hand in May, is Australia's main strike bowler, having taken 207 test wickets in 44 matches and was badly missed by Australia during recent unsuccessful tours of India and Sri Lanka.

The match against New South Wales in Sydney and another against South Australia from November 15 will be the only two chances Warne has to prove his fitness before Australia take on West Indies in the first test in Brisbane from November 22.
Warne will need to be near his prodigious best against a West Indies team likely to include at least three left-hand bastmen in world record holder Brian Lara, Shivnarine Chanderpaul and Jimmy Adams.
Left-handers are technically better equipped to cope with leg-spinners whose stock ball spins into them rather than away from right-handers.

Warne said his haul of seven wickets from a total of 20 overs in two recent interstate limited overs matches had been encouraging, but acknowledged that the real test of bowling successfully in long spells lay ahead of him.
"I think I'm ready, I've done all the work, and I've got 15 days to get myself right for the first test," Warne said.
"At this stage it's fantastic, so now it's time to get some wickets," he said.
